clue.text: Advice on food less useful after seeing girlfriend?

parts.note: food labelled best before a day is less good to eat after it
seeing a girlfriend is going out on a date

explanation.surface: A wry joke that romance spoils things: something loses its value once you've been out with your girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard label on packaged groceries advising buyers when quality starts to decline.

clue.text: Tasks in game for defenders that do the heavy lifting

definitions.meaning: in football or rugby, defenders ... opponents
a pulley-and-rope hoisting rig used to raise heavy loads

explanation.surface: Defenders are the team's workhorses, doing the heavy lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the first: the defenders who do the hard work, and also a hoisting rig.
explanation.definitionFit: Blocking and tackling are defensive duties in sport, and the same phrase names a pulley system for hoisting.

clue.text: Stigmas arising from small insult, mainly

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: Social stigmas that grow out of a minor slight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stigmas' suggests disgrace; here it is botanical, the pollen-catching tips of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice is the dried stigmas of the saffron crocus, so the definition names what it is made of.

clue.text: One smacked with the hand by head turning to leave

indicators.note: the slang word for head is turned round, reading backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for head
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone getting a slap round the head as they turn to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo is a small drum played by striking it with the hands rather than sticks.

clue.text: To set program up in stone is not serious enough

indicators.note: the turned program goes in, inside, the stone

parts.note: flint is a hard stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up means writing it upwards, so it reads backwards
this word means the letters it governs are turned round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A complaint that carving software into stone is too frivolous a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' and 'up' together give the reversal, split by the program word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant describes a lack of proper seriousness or respect, as with a glib remark.

clue.text: Royal couple's last to feast

parts.note: regal means royal

indicators.note: only the final letter of couple is wanted

explanation.surface: A royal couple's final banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale is to entertain lavishly, especially with food and drink, so it fits feasting.

clue.text: Organised parade: it's essentially different

indicators.note: organising the letters puts them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An observer remarking that this organised parade stands apart from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' looks like a pointer to the middle of 'it's', but all of 'it's' is in the anagram; 'essentially' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are fundamentally unlike one another, with no common basis.

clue.text: Racing colt finally put to stud, deprived of a run

indicators.note: only the last letter of colt is wanted
the earring word loses the letter for run

parts.note: a stud is a type of earring
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A racing colt retired to stud after losing a race, horse-breeding talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put to' just joins the pieces; the racing and stud imagery is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearing along means rushing at great speed, so tearing and racing are synonyms.

clue.text: Help me to get away to live with a French lady and cheerful dog

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
Mme is the abbreviation of Madame, a French lady
up means in good spirits
a Scotty is a Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: A plea for help to move away and live with a Frenchwoman and her happy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The catchphrase is from Star Trek, a request to be teleported out of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Trek line asks the engineer to teleport the speaker out, a plea to be rescued from a tight spot.

clue.text: Concerned with managing criminal behaviour

parts.note: 'of' can mean about or concerning, as in 'tales of adventure'
fending, as in fending for yourself, means managing or getting by

explanation.surface: A description of a job dealing with the management of criminals, such as probation work.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing crimes is called offending in legal and probation language, so it names unlawful conduct.

clue.text: Smooth ride at last after a modern vehicle's secured

indicators.note: the end of ride comes after the vehicle-and-a piece
the vehicle has secured the letter a, holding it inside itself

parts.note: an SUV, a sport utility vehicle, is a modern type of car

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word ride is wanted

explanation.surface: A car advert: a smooth ride, once you've got yourself a modern vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave and smooth are both used of a polished, urbane manner, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: An Australian native's at edge of outback in semi-desert

indicators.note: the a-and-roo piece sits at, right next to, the edge letter
the far edge of outback is its final letter

parts.note: an and a are both the indefinite article
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a native animal of Australia

explanation.surface: A kangaroo seen at the fringe of the Australian outback, in dry scrubland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian scene misleads: the Karoo is a semi-desert plateau region of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Karoo is a South African region of elevated arid plateaux, the standard example of semi-desert terrain.

clue.text: Paid after deduction of fine, this member of metal group

parts.words: Paid after deduction of fine, this
parts.note: fine is first-rate, written as an A and a figure one read as I; taking those two out of paid leaves the chemical symbol for the element, so 'this' is the element itself

explanation.surface: Like a payslip: what you were paid once a fine was docked, with a nod to metalworkers' unions.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate or fine, and in crosswords 1 often stands for I. The wordplay yields only the chemical symbol, and 'this' points from the symbol to the element it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Palladium is one of the platinum group metals, a set of six related elements in the periodic table.

clue.text: In game, stand at first behind square leg

indicators.note: the opening letter of stand goes behind, after, the square-leg piece

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

indicators.note: only the opening letter of stand is wanted

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a fielder told to stand behind square leg, a fielding position on the leg side level with the batter.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, but here 'square' gives NINE and 'leg' gives PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is a skittles game where nine wooden pins are bowled at, so it is a named game.

clue.text: Substantial bonus opera company received, gathering in wings of theatre

indicators.note: the bonus word receives the opera piece inside itself

parts.note: a plus is a bonus or extra

indicators.note: the opera company gathers in the wing letters, holding them inside

parts.note: ENO is English National Opera

indicators.note: the wings of theatre are its outermost letters

explanation.surface: An opera company gets a big bonus that brings people into the theatre's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenteous is an old-fashioned word for abundant or plentiful, meaning a large amount.

clue.text: Engineer's wide corner

parts.note: W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a wide
an angle is a corner where two lines meet

explanation.surface: An engineer's wide corner, like a broad bend in a road or a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a noun but is the verb, meaning to contrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle something is to obtain or arrange it by craft, just as one may engineer an outcome.

clue.text: Problem in hearing, wouldn't you say, workers organisations get round

indicators.note: the union letters get round the slang word, enclosing it

parts.note: TUs are trade unions, workers' organisations
innit is British slang for isn't it, a tag meaning wouldn't you say

explanation.surface: A union rep at a hearing who finds a way round a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests a tribunal; here it is the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is a medical condition causing ringing or buzzing in the ears.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying fuel requiring gentle handling

definitions.meaning: the wagon behind a steam locomotive that carries its coal and water
sore or delicate, as with a bruise that must be touched carefully

explanation.surface: A fuel tanker whose dangerous load must be handled carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam engine's coal truck has this name, and a sore or delicate spot is described the same way.

clue.text: Indifferent sound of original track one released

indicators.note: the word for original is heard, not spelt

parts.note: something original is new

indicators.note: the one is released, let out of the track word

parts.note: a trail is a track or path
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dull, flat sound from a track on a reissued record.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral means taking no side, so having no strong feeling either way.

clue.text: I have come in drunk to have a good time

indicators.note: the contraction comes into the slang phrase, sitting inside it

parts.note: lit up is slang for drunk
contracted, I have becomes I've

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they've staggered home drunk, all in the name of having fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to celebrate or enjoy oneself extravagantly, so it fits having fun.

clue.text: Sort of strength in steel when tempered

indicators.note: tempering changes steel's state, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Metallurgy: the strength steel acquires when it is tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Tensile strength is a material's resistance to breaking under tension.

clue.text: Firm having current and former coins

parts.note: firm and solid both mean hard and steady
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A firm that holds both modern and old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidi is the plural of solidus, the gold coin of the later Roman Empire.

clue.text: Matter less: it comes to nothing

parts.note: to count is to matter, as in 'every vote counts'
down means lower or less, as in 'profits are down'

explanation.surface: A shrug: it matters less, because it all amounts to nothing in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a launch count goes down to zero. Countdown is also the long-running British TV word-and-numbers quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence counting backwards ends at zero, so it literally arrives at nought.

clue.text: Curve is symbolically famous, where leader crashes out

indicators.note: the leading letter crashes out, dropping away from the front of the word

parts.note: something iconic is famous as a symbol of something

explanation.surface: A sporting curve of form: a famous side crashes out once its leader is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A conic is a conic section, the family of curves (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) cut from a cone.

clue.text: Nurse in working life losing some energy

indicators.note: the career word loses the energy letter

parts.note: a career is your working life
E is the physics symbol for energy; 'some' signals one of the two Es goes

explanation.surface: A nurse whose working life has left them somewhat drained.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone sick or disabled, so carer and nurse are close synonyms.

clue.text: Regular goalkeeper keeps moving slowly

indicators.note: the run of words regular goalkeeper keeps the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A first-choice goalkeeper who keeps moving slowly about the goalmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical tempo direction for a very slow, broad pace.

clue.text: Ban traveller at last in international order

indicators.note: that final letter goes in, inside, the decree word

parts.note: an edict is an official order or decree

indicators.note: only the final letter of traveller is wanted

explanation.surface: An international order barring a traveller, like a travel ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An interdict is a formal prohibition, especially a court order or church decree forbidding something.

clue.text: Cards offering credit lines to cover sharp rise in repair work

parts.note: credit cards are known collectively as plastic
a surge is a sudden sharp increase
RY, for railway, gives railway lines

explanation.surface: Paying for repairs on credit cards, with a sudden spike in the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic and reconstructive operations restore or remodel the body, so this surgery is a kind of repair.
